question: Najslávnejší upír nemého filmu, gróf Orlok z filmu Nosferatu, sídlil na skutočnom hrade na severe Slovenska. Ktorý je to hrad?
source_excerpt: all the exterior shots of Orlok's palace actually depict the 700-year-old Orava Castle that sits above the village of Oravský Podzámok

extra.why_interesting: Slovaks assume the world's most famous vampire film was shot in Transylvania or Germany. Its iconic vampire castle is actually one they may have visited on a school trip.
extra.verification_notes: Orava Castle in northern Slovakia is documented as the filming location for Orlok's castle exteriors in the 1922 Nosferatu (https://www.mentalfloss.com/entertainment/movies/11-nightmarish-facts-about-nosferatu).

explanation: Režisér Murnau v roku 1921 nakrúcal exteriéry upírovho sídla práve na Oravskom hrade, takže prvý veľký upírsky horor sveta je vlastne trochu slovenský. Hrad dodnes organizuje nočné prehliadky s Nosferatom.

question: Slávna slovenská pieseň Hej, Slováci má rovnakú melódiu ako štátna hymna jednej našej susednej krajiny. Ktorej?
source_excerpt: The melody is based on the Polish song Mazurek Dąbrowskiego (Poland Is Not Yet Lost), the national anthem of Poland.

extra.why_interesting: Slovaks treat 'Hej, Slováci' as a home-grown song. Few realise that their neighbours stand up for the same melody as their national anthem. A player can reason toward it: it must be a neighbouring Slavic country, and 'mazurka' rhythm points north.
extra.verification_notes: Hej, Slováci/Hej, Slované uses the melody of Mazurek Dąbrowskiego, the Polish national anthem; Poland borders Slovakia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hej,_Slované).

explanation: Samo Tomášik napísal svoj text na melódiu poľskej piesne Mazurek Dąbrowského, ktorá sa neskôr stala poľskou hymnou. Ten istý nápev dlhé roky slúžil aj ako hymna Juhoslávie.
